First, let's recall the following result:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+(kx)^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{k}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(kx)+C
$$

We proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{\sqrt{3}/6}\frac{1}{1+4{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{\sqrt{3}/6}\frac{1}{1+4{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{\sqrt{3}/6}\frac{1}{1+(2t)^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2t)]}_{a}^{\sqrt{3}/6} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2a)] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }(\frac{\pi }{6}-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2a)).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2x),$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2x)]=-\frac{\pi }{2}$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2x)]=\frac{\pi }{2}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14052212/assets/4612e37c6c611cbaa44c09f4dcc47d006ad45403fff9af5b4df7dca71693dd6e.png)

 

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{\sqrt{3}/6}\frac{1}{1+4{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }(\frac{\pi }{6}-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2a)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (\frac{\pi }{6}-(-\frac{\pi }{2})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
